HARBOUR LIGHTS FESTIVAL 2025
MASTER PLAN v4.2
Effective Date: 14 March 2025
Prepared by: Nadia Rahman, Festival Director
Status: CURRENT — Approved and in force until superseded by a later revision.

This Master Plan defines the overall vision, scope, dates, lineup, and key policies for Harbour Lights Festival 2025. It is the controlling document for all departments, vendors, and authorities. Any conflict between this plan and departmental documents must be escalated to the Festival Director’s office for resolution.

1. FESTIVAL VISION AND POSITIONING

Harbour Lights Festival returns for its ninth edition with the theme “Tides of Connection.” The festival celebrates Singapore’s maritime heritage and its role as a crossroads of cultures, bringing together local and regional artists across music, light art, and food. The waterfront setting is not a backdrop; it is central to the experience. Programming will use the harbour, the promenade, and the pier as distinct stages, with installations that respond to the movement of water and the changing skyline.

We aim to position Harbour Lights as Southeast Asia’s premier end-of-year waterfront festival, attracting 120,000 attendees across the three days. The audience mix targets 60% local residents and 40% international visitors, with a strong emphasis on repeat attendance and word-of-mouth advocacy.

2. SCHEDULED DATES

The Master Plan v4.2 lists the Harbour Lights Festival 2025 scheduled_dates as 2025-11-28, 2025-11-29, and 2025-11-30. Record status: current. These dates are confirmed and current; they are not provisional. No changes to the festival weekend are permitted without written approval from the Festival Director and the relevant authorities.

The dates fall on a Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This placement allows for a staggered build schedule and aligns with the school holiday period in Singapore. The Friday opening will feature a shorter programme (5:00 PM to 11:00 PM) to allow for final site readiness; Saturday and Sunday will run from 2:00 PM to midnight.

3. LINEUP AND PROGRAMMING

3.1 Headliners (Confirmed)

- Friday 28 November: RRILEY (SG) — Main Stage, 9:00 PM
- Saturday 29 November: The Midnight Collective (AU) — Main Stage, 9:30 PM
- Sunday 30 November: DJ Aisha (MY) — Main Stage, 9:00 PM

3.2 Supporting Acts (Confirmed)

- Friday: Local indie showcase featuring Lune, Paper Boats, and The Salty Dogs
- Saturday: Regional electronic acts (TBA final two slots by 15 April)
- Sunday: Acoustic sunset sessions on the Pier Stage

3.3 Light Art and Installations

Ten commissioned installations will be placed along the promenade and on the water. The centrepiece is “Beacon,” a 12-metre interactive light tower that responds to tidal data in real time. Installation build begins 24 November; all installations must be operational by 5:00 PM on 27 November for media preview.

3.4 Food and Market

The Harbour Market will host 40 food stalls and 25 artisan vendors. The food line-up emphasises coastal cuisines: Singapore seafood, Japanese street food, and Mediterranean mezze. Vendor applications close 30 June; contracts will be issued by 31 July.

4. CAPACITY AND ACCESS

- Total daily capacity: 40,000 attendees
- Main Stage area capacity: 18,000
- Pier Stage area capacity: 6,000
- Waterfront promenade: open access, no separate ticketing
- VIP and hospitality zones: 1,200 capacity per day

Capacity numbers are based on the latest crowd-density guidelines from the Singapore Civil Defence Force. Any change to the site layout that affects crowd flow must be re-approved by SCDF. The site plan in Appendix A is the approved version; no unauthorised modifications are permitted.

5. TICKETING AND PRICING

Ticketing tiers are as follows, in SGD:

- Early Bird (limited to 10,000 tickets): $98 per day
- Standard: $128 per day
- Weekend Pass (all three days): $298
- VIP Weekend Pass: $598
- Student and Senior Concession: $68 per day (valid identification required)

Tickets go on sale 1 May 2025 at 10:00 AM via the official ticketing platform. There will be no physical ticket sales at the gate. Re-entry is allowed until 10:00 PM each day with a valid wristband. Children under 12 enter free with a paying adult.
- Waste collection points are indicated on the site plan in Appendix A. Each point will be serviced every two hours during festival hours.
- All food vendors must use compostable packaging and cutlery. The Harbour Market will be monitored for compliance; vendors found using non-compliant packaging will be issued a warning, and repeat offences will result in a deduction from their stall deposit.
- Recycling bins will be colour-coded: blue for recyclables, green for compostables, and black for general waste. Crew and artist areas will have additional bins for e-waste.
- A post-event waste audit will be conducted on 2 December 2025. The findings will be published in the post-event report and used to inform the 2026 sustainability plan.

7. SAFETY AND SECURITY

7.1 Crowd Management

- The festival will operate under the crowd density parameters approved by the Singapore Civil Defence Force. The site plan in Appendix A reflects these parameters and is the only approved layout.
- A total of 180 safety personnel will be deployed across the three festival days, with an additional 60 on standby for the Saturday peak. Deployment zones are detailed in the Staffing Schedule (Appendix C).
- The Main Stage area will be divided into three zones (A, B, C) with separate entry and exit points. Zone capacity is monitored by the central control room using the live crowd-counting system.
- The Waterfront promenade will remain open access. However, if the promenade reaches 70% of its approved capacity, entry will be temporarily paused, and attendees will be directed to the holding area at Lot 7.
- A dedicated family area with a capacity of 800 will be located near the Pier Stage. This area is for attendees with children under 12 and includes a quiet zone and baby-care facilities.

7.2 Medical Services

- Two medical posts will be operational on site: Medical Post 1 near the Main Stage and Medical Post 2 near the Harbour Market. Each post will be staffed by at least two paramedics and one doctor during festival hours.
- An ambulance will be stationed at the festival site at all times. The ambulance will be located at the junction of the promenade and the Pier Stage access road.
- All medical incidents must be logged in the Incident Register, maintained by the Safety Office. The register will be reviewed daily by the Festival Director and the Safety Manager.
- Heat exhaustion and dehydration protocols will be in effect. Free water refill stations are located at 10 points across the site, and signage will direct attendees to these stations.

The Master Plan v4.2 notes that Nadia Rahman approval_status_for_master_plan_v4.2 is approved. Record status: current.

7.3 Security

- Security screening will be conducted at all entry points. Bag checks and metal detector scans will be in place from the opening of gates each day.
- A total of 90 security personnel will be deployed, with additional officers assigned to the artist backstage area and the VIP zones.
- The backstage area is restricted to authorised personnel only. Access will be controlled by a wristband system, with different colours indicating different levels of access. Lost or damaged wristbands must be reported to the Security Office immediately; replacements will be issued only after identity verification.
- A lost-and-found office will be located at the Visitor Services tent, near the main entrance.

8. ARTIST AND PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT

8.1 Artist Arrival and Hospitality

- Artist arrival times are detailed in the Run Sheet (Appendix D). All artists must arrive at the artist entrance (Gate A) at least 90 minutes before their scheduled set time.
- Each artist will be assigned a dedicated production manager from the festival team. The production manager will coordinate sound checks, technical requirements, and hospitality.
- Backstage hospitality will include a green room with catering, a private rest area, and a dressing room. Catering will be provided by the festival's official caterer, with vegetarian, vegan, and halal options available.
- Artist riders must be submitted to the Production Office by 1 November 2025. Riders received after this date will be accommodated where possible but cannot be guaranteed.
- All artists must complete a technical rider and stage plot by 1 October 2025. These documents are required for the final sound and lighting design.
8.2 Stage and Lineup Management

- The festival will operate three stages: the Main Stage, the Sentosa Stage, and the Bayfront Acoustic Stage. Each stage will have a dedicated stage manager reporting to the Production Director.
- Stage schedules are published in the Run Sheet (Appendix D). Set times are fixed once approved and will not be adjusted for individual artist preferences. Any proposed change must be submitted in writing to the Production Office no later than 48 hours before the affected performance.
- The Main Stage will feature six performances per day, with the headliner closing the evening. The Sentosa Stage will feature eight performances per day, with a longer format for the headliner act to allow for a production-heavy set.
- The Bayfront Acoustic Stage will feature continuous performances from 12:00 to 22:00, with shorter set times and minimal technical requirements.

8.2.1 Sentosa Stage Headliner

- The Master Plan v4.2 lists The Sentosa Stage headliner_act as The Cosmic Keys. Record status: current. This designation is current and applies to all three festival days.
- The Cosmic Keys will perform a single continuous set each day, with a scheduled duration of 90 minutes. The set will commence at 21:00 on Friday and Saturday, and at 20:30 on Sunday to allow for the earlier site closure.
- The Cosmic Keys will require the following technical provisions, as confirmed in their technical rider dated 1 September 2025:
  - Full backline as specified in the rider, including two keyboard rigs and a modular synth setup.
  - A lighting package of 24 moving heads and 8 strobes, with a dedicated lighting operator.
  - In-ear monitoring for all band members. Wedge monitors will be available as a backup.
  - A private green room adjacent to the Sentosa Stage, with capacity for 12 people.
- The Cosmic Keys will arrive at Gate A at 19:00 each day. Their production manager will escort them to the backstage area. Sound check is scheduled from 19:30 to 20:30.
- No encore is planned. The set will end at the scheduled time to allow for the stage changeover to the following day's configuration.

8.2.2 Main Stage Headliner

- The Main Stage headliner for all three nights is the band Meridian Halo. This booking was confirmed under the original artist agreement dated 12 March 2025 and remains unchanged in the current plan.
- Meridian Halo will perform a 105-minute set each night, commencing at 21:30. Their technical requirements are detailed in the Main Stage Production Schedule (Appendix E).

8.2.3 Bayfront Acoustic Stage

- The Bayfront Acoustic Stage will feature local and regional artists, with a focus on singer-songwriters and small ensembles. The full lineup is listed in Appendix F.
- Performances on this stage will not require a full production team. Each artist will be provided with a sound engineer and a stage assistant.

9. TICKETING AND CAPACITY

9.1 Ticket Categories and Pricing

- Standard Weekend Pass: SGD 188 (includes entry to all three days)
- Single-Day Pass: SGD 78 per day
- VIP Weekend Pass: SGD 420 (includes access to the VIP lounge, dedicated viewing areas at the Main Stage and Sentosa Stage, and complimentary refreshments)
- Group Pass (4 or more): SGD 168 per person for a Weekend Pass
- All tickets are subject to a SGD 4 booking fee per transaction. Prices are inclusive of GST.

9.2 Capacity and Entry

- The maximum daily capacity for the festival site is 18,000 attendees. This figure includes all ticket holders, staff, artists, and accredited media.
- The Sentosa Stage viewing area will have a capacity of 5,000 attendees. Access will be on a first-come, first-served basis, with no re-entry once the area has reached capacity.
- The VIP lounge will have a capacity of 400 attendees at any one time.
- All attendees must present a valid ticket and a government-issued photo identification for entry. Tickets are non-transferable and non-refundable.

9.3 Ticketing Sales Windows

- Early Bird Weekend Passes (SGD 158) will be available from 15 April 2025 to 30 April 2025, or until sold out.
- General sales open on 1 May 2025.
- All ticket sales will close at 23:59 on 26 November 2025, or when the event sells out, whichever occurs first.
## HARBOUR LIGHTS FESTIVAL 2025
### MASTER PLAN — REVISION 4 (30 SEPTEMBER 2025)

**Prepared by:** Festival Director’s Office
**Approved by:** Nadia Rahman, Festival Director
**Date of Issue:** 30 September 2025
**Status:** Current. Supersedes Revision 3 (5 August 2025). All departments, vendors, and authorities are to operate in accordance with this revision unless a specific section is noted otherwise.

#### 10. ENTRY, SECURITY, AND SAFETY

**10.1 Entry Procedures**

- All gates will open at 15:00 on Friday, 28 November 2025, and at 10:00 on Saturday and Sunday, 29–30 November 2025. Gate closing times will be 22:30 on Friday and 21:30 on Saturday and Sunday.
- Attendees must pass through security screening at the designated entry points. Prohibited items include, but are not limited to: outside food and beverages, glass containers, aerosols, laser pointers, fireworks, and any item that may be used as a projectile.
- Bag checks will be conducted at all entry points. Bags larger than 30cm x 40cm x 20cm will not be permitted into the festival site. A bag storage service will be available at a fee of SGD 8 per item per day.
- Re-entry to the festival site is permitted only with a Weekend Pass. Single-Day Pass holders may not leave and re-enter the site on the same day.
- Lost or stolen tickets will not be replaced unless purchased through the official ticketing agent with purchase protection. Attendees are advised to keep their tickets on their person at all times.

**10.2 Security Personnel and Crowd Management**

- A total of 180 security personnel will be deployed across the festival site, with 60 personnel per shift. This figure includes uniformed officers, plainclothes operatives, and control room staff.
- Crowd density in the Main Stage viewing area will be monitored in real time. If density reaches 80% of the area’s safe capacity, entry to the viewing area will be temporarily paused until density falls below 75%.
- The Sentosa Stage viewing area, with a capacity of 5,000 attendees, will be managed separately. Marshals will be stationed at all entry and exit points of this area.
- Any attendee found to be in possession of a prohibited item will be asked to dispose of the item or leave the site. Refusal to comply will result in ejection without refund.

**10.3 Emergency Procedures**

- In the event of a lightning warning issued by the National Environment Agency, all outdoor stages will pause performances immediately. Attendees will be directed to the nearest covered shelter. Performances will resume no earlier than 30 minutes after the all-clear is given.
- Medical posts will be located at the following points: Main Stage rear, Bayfront Acoustic Stage side, Sentosa Stage entry plaza, and the central food village. Each post will be staffed by at least two certified first-aid personnel during operating hours.
- A lost-and-found station will operate at the Festival Information Booth from 15:00 to 23:00 daily.

---

#### 11. SUSTAINABILITY AND SITE MANAGEMENT

**11.1 Waste and Recycling**

- The festival will operate a three-bin system throughout the site: general waste, recyclables, and food waste. Bins will be cleared at minimum every two hours during operating hours.
- All food and beverage vendors are required to use compostable or recyclable packaging. Vendors who fail to comply will be subject to a SGD 200 fine per violation, deducted from their settlement.
- At the close of each festival day, the site will be cleared of all waste. A post-event waste audit will be conducted and reported to the Land Transport Authority as part of the event’s environmental commitment.

**11.2 Water and Power**

- Potable water refill stations will be available at four locations across the site. Attendees are encouraged to bring reusable bottles.
- Generators will be silenced between 23:00 and 07:00 except for essential security and medical equipment. Noise levels at the site boundary will be maintained below 65 dB(A) during this period.
- The festival will offset 100% of its estimated carbon emissions through the purchase of certified carbon credits. The offset certificate will be displayed at the Festival Information Booth.

HARBOUR LIGHTS FESTIVAL 2025
MASTER PLAN v4.2
Effective Date: 14 March 2025
Prepared by: Nadia Rahman, Festival Director
Status: CURRENT — Approved and in force until superseded by a later revision.

This Master Plan defines the overall vision, scope, dates, lineup, and key policies for Harbour Lights Festival 2025. It is the controlling document for all departments, vendors, and authorities. Any conflict between this plan and departmental documents must be escalated to the Festival Director’s office for resolution.

1. FESTIVAL VISION AND POSITIONING

Harbour Lights Festival returns for its ninth edition with the theme “Tides of Connection.” The festival celebrates Singapore’s maritime heritage and its role as a crossroads of cultures, bringing together local and regional artists across music, light art, and food. The waterfront setting is not a backdrop; it is central to the experience. Programming will use the harbour, the promenade, and the pier as distinct stages, with installations that respond to the movement of water and the changing skyline.

We aim to position Harbour Lights as Southeast Asia’s premier end-of-year waterfront festival, attracting 120,000 attendees across the three days. The audience mix targets 60% local residents and 40% international visitors, with a strong emphasis on repeat attendance and word-of-mouth advocacy.

2. SCHEDULED DATES

The Master Plan v4.2 lists the Harbour Lights Festival 2025 scheduled_dates as 2025-11-28, 2025-11-29, and 2025-11-30. Record status: current. These dates are confirmed and current; they are not provisional. No changes to the festival weekend are permitted without written approval from the Festival Director and the relevant authorities.

The dates fall on a Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This placement allows for a staggered build schedule and aligns with the school holiday period in Singapore. The Friday opening will feature a shorter programme (5:00 PM to 11:00 PM) to allow for final site readiness; Saturday and Sunday will run from 2:00 PM to midnight.

3. LINEUP AND PROGRAMMING

3.1 Headliners (Confirmed)

- Friday 28 November: RRILEY (SG) — Main Stage, 9:00 PM
- Saturday 29 November: The Midnight Collective (AU) — Main Stage, 9:30 PM
- Sunday 30 November: DJ Aisha (MY) — Main Stage, 9:00 PM

3.2 Supporting Acts (Confirmed)

- Friday: Local indie showcase featuring Lune, Paper Boats, and The Salty Dogs
- Saturday: Regional electronic acts (TBA final two slots by 15 April)
- Sunday: Acoustic sunset sessions on the Pier Stage

3.3 Light Art and Installations

Ten commissioned installations will be placed along the promenade and on the water. The centrepiece is “Beacon,” a 12-metre interactive light tower that responds to tidal data in real time. Installation build begins 24 November; all installations must be operational by 5:00 PM on 27 November for media preview.

3.4 Food and Market

The Harbour Market will host 40 food stalls and 25 artisan vendors. The food line-up emphasises coastal cuisines: Singapore seafood, Japanese street food, and Mediterranean mezze. Vendor applications close 30 June; contracts will be issued by 31 July.

4. CAPACITY AND ACCESS

- Total daily capacity: 40,000 attendees
- Main Stage area capacity: 18,000
- Pier Stage area capacity: 6,000
- Waterfront promenade: open access, no separate ticketing
- VIP and hospitality zones: 1,200 capacity per day

Capacity numbers are based on the latest crowd-density guidelines from the Singapore Civil Defence Force. Any change to the site layout that affects crowd flow must be re-approved by SCDF. The site plan in Appendix A is the approved version; no unauthorised modifications are permitted.

5. TICKETING AND PRICING

Ticketing tiers are as follows, in SGD:

- Early Bird (limited to 10,000 tickets): $98 per day
- Standard: $128 per day
- Weekend Pass (all three days): $298
- VIP Weekend Pass: $598
- Student and Senior Concession: $68 per day (valid identification required)

Tickets go on sale 1 May 2025 at 10:00 AM via the official ticketing platform. There will be no physical ticket sales at the gate. Re-entry is allowed until 10:00 PM each day with a valid wristband. Children under 12 enter free with a paying adult.

- Waste collection points are indicated on the site plan in Appendix A. Each point will be serviced every two hours during festival hours.
- All food vendors must use compostable packaging and cutlery. The Harbour Market will be monitored for compliance; vendors found using non-compliant packaging will be issued a warning, and repeat offences will result in a deduction from their stall deposit.
- Recycling bins will be colour-coded: blue for recyclables, green for compostables, and black for general waste. Crew and artist areas will have additional bins for e-waste.
- A post-event waste audit will be conducted on 2 December 2025. The findings will be published in the post-event report and used to inform the 2026 sustainability plan.

7. SAFETY AND SECURITY

7.1 Crowd Management

- The festival will operate under the crowd density parameters approved by the Singapore Civil Defence Force. The site plan in Appendix A reflects these parameters and is the only approved layout.
- A total of 180 safety personnel will be deployed across the three festival days, with an additional 60 on standby for the Saturday peak. Deployment zones are detailed in the Staffing Schedule (Appendix C).
- The Main Stage area will be divided into three zones (A, B, C) with separate entry and exit points. Zone capacity is monitored by the central control room using the live crowd-counting system.
- The Waterfront promenade will remain open access. However, if the promenade reaches 70% of its approved capacity, entry will be temporarily paused, and attendees will be directed to the holding area at Lot 7.
- A dedicated family area with a capacity of 800 will be located near the Pier Stage. This area is for attendees with children under 12 and includes a quiet zone and baby-care facilities.

7.2 Medical Services

- Two medical posts will be operational on site: Medical Post 1 near the Main Stage and Medical Post 2 near the Harbour Market. Each post will be staffed by at least two paramedics and one doctor during festival hours.
- An ambulance will be stationed at the festival site at all times. The ambulance will be located at the junction of the promenade and the Pier Stage access road.
- All medical incidents must be logged in the Incident Register, maintained by the Safety Office. The register will be reviewed daily by the Festival Director and the Safety Manager.
- Heat exhaustion and dehydration protocols will be in effect. Free water refill stations are located at 10 points across the site, and signage will direct attendees to these stations.

7.3 Security

- Security screening will be conducted at all entry points. Bag checks and metal detector scans will be in place from the opening of gates each day.
- A total of 90 security personnel will be deployed, with additional officers assigned to the artist backstage area and the VIP zones.
- The backstage area is restricted to authorised personnel only. Access will be controlled by a wristband system, with different colours indicating different levels of access. Lost or damaged wristbands must be reported to the Security Office immediately; replacements will be issued only after identity verification.
- A lost-and-found office will be located at the Visitor Services tent, near the main entrance.

8. ARTIST AND PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT

8.1 Artist Arrival and Hospitality

- Artist arrival times are detailed in the Run Sheet (Appendix D). All artists must arrive at the artist entrance (Gate A) at least 90 minutes before their scheduled set time.
- Each artist will be assigned a dedicated production manager from the festival team. The production manager will coordinate sound checks, technical requirements, and hospitality.
- Backstage hospitality will include a green room with catering, a private rest area, and a dressing room. Catering will be provided by the festival's official caterer, with vegetarian, vegan, and halal options available.
- Artist riders must be submitted to the Production Office by 1 November 2025. Riders received after this date will be accommodated where possible but cannot be guaranteed.
- All artists must complete a technical rider and stage plot by 1 October 2025. These documents are required for the final sound and lighting design.

documents.content:
8.2 Stage and Lineup Management

- The festival will operate three stages: the Main Stage, the Sentosa Stage, and the Bayfront Acoustic Stage. Each stage will have a dedicated stage manager reporting to the Production Director.
- Stage schedules are published in the Run Sheet (Appendix D). Set times are fixed once approved and will not be adjusted for individual artist preferences. Any proposed change must be submitted in writing to the Production Office no later than 48 hours before the affected performance.
- The Main Stage will feature six performances per day, with the headliner closing the evening. The Sentosa Stage will feature eight performances per day, with a longer format for the headliner act to allow for a production-heavy set.
- The Bayfront Acoustic Stage will feature continuous performances from 12:00 to 22:00, with shorter set times and minimal technical requirements.

8.2.1 Sentosa Stage Headliner

- The Master Plan v4.2 lists The Sentosa Stage headliner_act as The Cosmic Keys. Record status: current. This designation is current and applies to all three festival days.
- The Cosmic Keys will perform a single continuous set each day, with a scheduled duration of 90 minutes. The set will commence at 21:00 on Friday and Saturday, and at 20:30 on Sunday to allow for the earlier site closure.
- The Cosmic Keys will require the following technical provisions, as confirmed in their technical rider dated 1 September 2025:
  - Full backline as specified in the rider, including two keyboard rigs and a modular synth setup.
  - A lighting package of 24 moving heads and 8 strobes, with a dedicated lighting operator.
  - In-ear monitoring for all band members. Wedge monitors will be available as a backup.
  - A private green room adjacent to the Sentosa Stage, with capacity for 12 people.
- The Cosmic Keys will arrive at Gate A at 19:00 each day. Their production manager will escort them to the backstage area. Sound check is scheduled from 19:30 to 20:30.
- No encore is planned. The set will end at the scheduled time to allow for the stage changeover to the following day's configuration.

8.2.2 Main Stage Headliner

- The Main Stage headliner for all three nights is the band Meridian Halo. This booking was confirmed under the original artist agreement dated 12 March 2025 and remains unchanged in the current plan.
- Meridian Halo will perform a 105-minute set each night, commencing at 21:30. Their technical requirements are detailed in the Main Stage Production Schedule (Appendix E).

8.2.3 Bayfront Acoustic Stage

- The Bayfront Acoustic Stage will feature local and regional artists, with a focus on singer-songwriters and small ensembles. The full lineup is listed in Appendix F.
- Performances on this stage will not require a full production team. Each artist will be provided with a sound engineer and a stage assistant.

9. TICKETING AND CAPACITY

9.1 Ticket Categories and Pricing

- Standard Weekend Pass: SGD 188 (includes entry to all three days)
- Single-Day Pass: SGD 78 per day
- VIP Weekend Pass: SGD 420 (includes access to the VIP lounge, dedicated viewing areas at the Main Stage and Sentosa Stage, and complimentary refreshments)
- Group Pass (4 or more): SGD 168 per person for a Weekend Pass
- All tickets are subject to a SGD 4 booking fee per transaction. Prices are inclusive of GST.

9.2 Capacity and Entry

- The maximum daily capacity for the festival site is 18,000 attendees. This figure includes all ticket holders, staff, artists, and accredited media.
- The Sentosa Stage viewing area will have a capacity of 5,000 attendees. Access will be on a first-come, first-served basis, with no re-entry once the area has reached capacity.
- The VIP lounge will have a capacity of 400 attendees at any one time.
- All attendees must present a valid ticket and a government-issued photo identification for entry. Tickets are non-transferable and non-refundable.

9.3 Ticketing Sales Windows

- Early Bird Weekend Passes (SGD 158) will be available from 15 April 2025 to 30 April 2025, or until sold out.
- General sales open on 1 May 2025.
- All ticket sales will close at 23:59 on 26 November 2025, or when the event sells out, whichever occurs first.

## HARBOUR LIGHTS FESTIVAL 2025
### MASTER PLAN — REVISION 4 (30 SEPTEMBER 2025)

**Prepared by:** Festival Director’s Office
**Approved by:** Nadia Rahman, Festival Director
**Date of Issue:** 30 September 2025
**Status:** Current. Supersedes Revision 3 (5 August 2025). All departments, vendors, and authorities are to operate in accordance with this revision unless a specific section is noted otherwise.

---

#### 10. ENTRY, SECURITY, AND SAFETY

**10.1 Entry Procedures**

- All gates will open at 15:00 on Friday, 28 November 2025, and at 10:00 on Saturday and Sunday, 29–30 November 2025. Gate closing times will be 22:30 on Friday and 21:30 on Saturday and Sunday.
- Attendees must pass through security screening at the designated entry points. Prohibited items include, but are not limited to: outside food and beverages, glass containers, aerosols, laser pointers, fireworks, and any item that may be used as a projectile.
- Bag checks will be conducted at all entry points. Bags larger than 30cm x 40cm x 20cm will not be permitted into the festival site. A bag storage service will be available at a fee of SGD 8 per item per day.
- Re-entry to the festival site is permitted only with a Weekend Pass. Single-Day Pass holders may not leave and re-enter the site on the same day.
- Lost or stolen tickets will not be replaced unless purchased through the official ticketing agent with purchase protection. Attendees are advised to keep their tickets on their person at all times.

**10.2 Security Personnel and Crowd Management**

- A total of 180 security personnel will be deployed across the festival site, with 60 personnel per shift. This figure includes uniformed officers, plainclothes operatives, and control room staff.
- Crowd density in the Main Stage viewing area will be monitored in real time. If density reaches 80% of the area’s safe capacity, entry to the viewing area will be temporarily paused until density falls below 75%.
- The Sentosa Stage viewing area, with a capacity of 5,000 attendees, will be managed separately. Marshals will be stationed at all entry and exit points of this area.
- Any attendee found to be in possession of a prohibited item will be asked to dispose of the item or leave the site. Refusal to comply will result in ejection without refund.

**10.3 Emergency Procedures**

- In the event of a lightning warning issued by the National Environment Agency, all outdoor stages will pause performances immediately. Attendees will be directed to the nearest covered shelter. Performances will resume no earlier than 30 minutes after the all-clear is given.
- Medical posts will be located at the following points: Main Stage rear, Bayfront Acoustic Stage side, Sentosa Stage entry plaza, and the central food village. Each post will be staffed by at least two certified first-aid personnel during operating hours.
- A lost-and-found station will operate at the Festival Information Booth from 15:00 to 23:00 daily.

---

#### 11. SUSTAINABILITY AND SITE MANAGEMENT

**11.1 Waste and Recycling**

- The festival will operate a three-bin system throughout the site: general waste, recyclables, and food waste. Bins will be cleared at minimum every two hours during operating hours.
- All food and beverage vendors are required to use compostable or recyclable packaging. Vendors who fail to comply will be subject to a SGD 200 fine per violation, deducted from their settlement.
- At the close of each festival day, the site will be cleared of all waste. A post-event waste audit will be conducted and reported to the Land Transport Authority as part of the event’s environmental commitment.

**11.2 Water and Power**

- Potable water refill stations will be available at four locations across the site. Attendees are encouraged to bring reusable bottles.
- Generators will be silenced between 23:00 and 07:00 except for essential security and medical equipment. Noise levels at the site boundary will be maintained below 65 dB(A) during this period.
- The festival will offset 100% of its estimated carbon emissions through the purchase of certified carbon credits. The offset certificate will be displayed at the Festival Information Booth.

4. MERLION STAGE (ST-01) – GENERAL DESCRIPTION

The Merlion Stage is the principal performance venue of the festival. It is designed to accommodate a full band or orchestra, with support for aerial acts, pyrotechnics, and a large LED screen wall.

4.1 Stage Orientation (Current Specification)

The stage design brief v2 specifies that The Merlion Stage stage_orientation is facing south-west. Record status: current. This orientation is current and controlled. All sightlines, camera positions, and audience flow plans in this document assume this facing.

Rationale for orientation: South-west facing positions the stage against the Marina Bay skyline as the backdrop, with the Merlion statue visible to the left of the audience area. This provides a visually distinctive frame for broadcast and still photography. The orientation also places the stage upwind of the main audience area during the prevailing north-east monsoon transition period, reducing smoke and haze drift from effects into the crowd.
